subject: First day check
body:
Good luck on your first day.

If the inbox starts screaming, breathe and sort the customer mail first. Call me before midnight, you promised.

subject: The first night
body:
The first night is always quiet. Nobody has been here long enough to bring anything with them.

Read the rest of the mail, plan tomorrow (the builder locks now, that is the licence, not me) and then go to bed. The room behind the office is yours: the door by the key board. The bed is made and the alarm is set for half past six. If the little television only shows the test card, it is late.

If the main trips in the night, the board is in the generator shed and Novotny's number is on the noticeboard. He moans after nine. Let him.

- V.

subject: The radio
body:
Leave the radio in the office playing at night. Your uncle said the guests sleep better when they can hear it from the tents.

I think he meant himself.

- V.

subject: Tariff reminder
body:
Your account is billed nightly at 20:00 local.

Unpaid invoices carry a three day grace period. After that the supply is interrupted and the backup unit in the office will hold the site for approximately six minutes.

This message is automated.

subject: Occupancy scan
body:
Automated report:
- Mail feed active
- Occupancy scan complete
- 1 occupied unit without an assigned guest ID

Ticket closed automatically. No action required.

subject: Photo from town
body:
I walked past the old bus stop. It looks exactly like the wallpaper on your camp computer. Same bench, same sign.

Who took that photo?

subject: Water meter note
body:
Quick note: the old water meter drifts at night. If guests complain, tell them we are scheduling service.

It drifted all winter, with the camp shut and nobody here to use a drop. Nobody is scheduling anything.

subject: count them
body:
you counted them at check-in

count them again after 22:00

the number is not the same

subject: Night log
body:
02:58  gate closed
03:00  all guests accounted for
03:01  operator asleep at desk

No incidents.

subject: Kemp Cerne jezero: inspection of operation
body:
Dear operator,

We confirm that the inspection of the operation of the facility Kemp Cerne jezero (parcel 412/3) will take place on Monday 19 October 1998 at 8:00.

The application of Agrostroj Hlubocany a.s. for a change of land use remains with the District Office. Should the facility not be in operation on the date of inspection, the Office will recommend the change.

This letter is for your information. No reply is required.

Ing. Pokorny
Department of Land Use

subject: Socks
body:
You were up late again. The grey socks are in the second drawer, the office floor is cold in the morning.

- V.

subject: Settlement batch cleared
body: Settlement batch cleared. One guest record could not be matched to a payment and was carried over.

subject: (no subject)
body:
The lamp by the lake was on all night. Good. Keep it on.

Do not walk along the fence after the lamps go out. Your uncle did.

- V.

subject: Call me
body:
You did not call. That is fine. I called the camp number instead and somebody picked up and listened for a while.

Was that you?

subject: Our offer stands
body:
Dear owner,

Our offer for the land at Cerne jezero stands: 2.4 million crowns, paid at signature. The structures would of course be removed at our cost, the lake left as it is for the cooling water.

We understand the camp has been closed since last summer. Nobody will blame you for selling. Mr Karel H. was close to signing with us last autumn, before the accident.

With respect,
J. Maly, commercial director

subject: Tuesdays
body:
My sister's grandson lets me use his computer on Tuesdays. Everyone in this house is very old.

I hear you have guests. Good. Write them all in the book, even the ones who do not give a name.

If you find a little red shoe anywhere, leave it where it is. Do not bring it in.

- V.

subject: Tomorrow
body: The inspection is tomorrow, right? Whatever they say, I kept your seat on the bus.

subject: Tomorrow at eight
body:
The man from the district comes at eight. I will come out on the first bus and stand next to you; he knew your uncle.

Leave the books on the desk and the terminal on.

I will count them myself.

- Teta Vera
